summary: win32CreationTimeSource.read returns the creation time of a process that has already exited but is still held open by another handle, because it never checks the exit time or exit code. The PowerShell Win32_Process query it replaces returned '' for exited processes. The terminal-agent owner watchdog (terminal-agent.ts:1187) treats a matching start time as 'owner alive' and never checks liveness, so an agent can outlive a crashed browse server: the Windows terminal-agent leak this area guards against.
evidence: read(): `if (!GetProcessTimes(...) || times[0] === 0n) return; return `/Date(${times[0]/10_000n - EPOCH})/`` ignores times[1] (exit time). terminal-agent.ts:1187: `if (!BROWSE_OWNER_START_TIME || readAgentStartTime(BROWSE_OWNER_PID) !== BROWSE_OWNER_START_TIME || ...) void cleanup();` has no isProcessAlive check. readAgentStartTime now returns `win32CreationTimeSource.read(pid) ?? windowsProcessQuery(pid).startTime`. Not run, because this is a Linux host; fix by returning undefined when times[1] !== 0n or GetExitCodeProcess != STILL_ACTIVE (259).
